summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of international travel finances, including forex cards, zero-markup credit cards, cash, and TCS rules. However, some specific details regarding the effective date of IDFC FIRST Bank's zero-markup policy and the current TCS applicability on international credit card spending need correction or clarification.

claims.claim: Be aware of the updated Tax Collected at Source (TCS) rules, effective April 1, 2026, impacting overseas remittances and tour packages.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the effective date of April 1, 2026, for the updated TCS rules.

claims.claim: Effective April 1, 2026, for remittances *other than* overseas tour packages, there will be no Tax Collected at Source (TCS) on amounts up to ₹10 lakh per financial year. A TCS of 20% will be applicable on amounts exceeding this ₹10 lakh threshold.
claims.note: This is consistently stated across multiple authoritative sources for 'other LRS purposes' (excluding tour packages, education, and medical).

claims.claim: IDFC FIRST Bank (which announced 0% forex markup across its credit cards from September 2026)
claims.note: IDFC FIRST Bank announced the removal of forex markup across all its credit cards effective September 2026 (specifically September 9, 2026, as per some sources).

claims.claim: The Indian government, through the Income-tax Act, 1961 (and subsequently section 394 of the Income-tax Act, 2025), mandates Tax Collected at Source (TCS) on certain foreign remittances made under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
claims.note: Section 206C of the Income-tax Act, 1961, has been consolidated into Section 394 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, effective April 1, 2026.

claims.claim: For payments made for overseas tour packages, a flat 2% TCS will be applicable from the first rupee, with no threshold.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm a flat 2% TCS on overseas tour packages from April 1, 2026, with no threshold.

claims.claim: International credit card spending abroad is currently deferred from LRS inclusion and does not attract TCS.
claims.note: Several sources confirm that the inclusion of international credit card spending under LRS for TCS purposes has been deferred, meaning it currently does not attract TCS.

claims.claim: The LRS allows resident individuals to remit up to USD 250,000 (approximately ₹2 crore) per financial year (April to March) for various permissible current or capital account transactions, including travel, education, medical treatment, and investments.
claims.note: The RBI and other financial portals confirm the LRS limit of USD 250,000 per financial year for resident individuals.

article_title: Optimising Your International Travel Budget: Cards, Cash & Forex
